key_insight: RS-JEPA proposes a compact self-supervised approach to matching remote sensing images across different sensor types. It uses joint-embedding prediction with scan-path views to learn representations for cross-sensor retrieval.
problem_solved: Finding scenes with the same content across SAR–optical or panchromatic–multispectral imagery without manual labels, while addressing limitations of pixel reconstruction, co-registered-pair-only alignment, and large transformer models.
method: Use a joint-embedding predictive framework to learn image representations for cross-sensor retrieval.
Incorporate scan-path views, as indicated by the paper title; their construction is not described in the supplied abstract.
Target a compact architecture rather than the large transformers used by some existing methods; exact architecture and parameter counts are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach could support label-free search across heterogeneous satellite image archives with a smaller model. Retrieval accuracy and efficiency gains cannot be assessed from the supplied excerpt.

paper_title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
paper_authors: Tanishq Rachamalla, Srishti Kaushik, Muhammad Attique Khan, Gustau Camps-Valls, Swalpa Kumar Roy
